record_status_text: draft, pending confirmation by both owners
drafted_by: An AI coding agent, for Putu and Rachmania to read, correct and confirm. The team rule is: agents draft, humans sign. This draft is not a decision and gives nobody a right to use anything.
what_this_is: A rights record says which terms of use, which credit line and which change notice apply to one outside data source, and whether both project owners have confirmed that. This one is for the two Sentinel-1 radar scenes that the team's own flood candidates of case O1 are made from. Until both owners confirm it and it is added to the rights registry, the code refuses every O1 candidate, exactly as it did before this file existed.
source: Copernicus Sentinel-1A Level-1 GRD scenes of 3 and 15 September 2024 over Mae Sai (IW mode, VV and VH, descending pass, relative orbit 135): the image pair of the own radar candidates of case O1

radar_receipt.what_it_gives: The file name, SHA-256 and size of both archives (inputs.pre_event_safe, inputs.post_event_safe), the two acquisition times and the time in Thailand (source_timestamps). It is the receipt of the run of record of plan tasks A2 and A4.

sensitivity_receipt.what_it_gives: The same two archives with the same SHA-256 and size. The sensitivity run reads nothing else from Sentinel-1.

acquisition_manifest_in_git.what_it_gives: Both product names, both catalogue product ids, the same SHA-256 and size for each archive, and the column source_license_status with the value confirmed_copernicus_sentinel_legal_notice. It marks download_attempted False for both archives, gives retrieved_at_utc 2026-07-20T07:00:00Z and names nobody who downloaded them.

acquisition_manifest_outside_git.note: The radar receipt names a copy of the manifest outside Git with this SHA-256. It is another file than the committed manifest. It was not read for this draft; the radar receipt says that it gives the same SHA-256 for both archives.

terms_as_the_repository_records_them.term: Data passed on or shown unchanged carry the credit: Copernicus Sentinel data 2024. Adapted or modified data carry the credit: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024.
The notice gives no warranty that the data are fit for a purpose. It does not establish scientific validity or fitness for emergency decisions.
On the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, Sentinel product data are governed by the Sentinel legal notice; other content of the portal has its own terms.

The project's own register of 23 September 2026 lists the Mae Sai pair as allowed for the existing documented research processing scope, says that candidate derivatives are subject to the Copernicus notice and to package export checks, and calls itself an engineering register, not a legal clearance.

change_notice.template: Changed by FloodGuard: calibrated to sigma0 ({calibration}); geocoded ({geocoding}); resampled to {cell_size_m} m cells in {target_crs}; cut to {frame}; the scenes of {pre_event_date} and {post_event_date} compared and classified by {method} into a flood candidate. Tier 2 own candidate: verify before action. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024.

steps.text: Say how the pixel values were calibrated. In the runs of 4 October 2026: sigma0 from the sigmaNought table of the product; thermal noise not removed; no orbit file applied.

Name the geocoding and say so where it is approximate. In the run of record: the product's ground control points fitted by GDAL's second-order polynomial, with no terrain model; the layers are displaced by about 680 m (open point A4-OP1).
Give the cell size, the coordinate system and the resampling method. In the runs: 10 m cells in EPSG:32647, bilinear on linear sigma0.
Say what the layer was cut to. In the runs: the eight Mae Sai tambons of protocol v1a.
Give the two dates, the method and its parameters: the UN-SPIDER practice with its ratio of 1.25, M1-literal, or the frozen M1-v2.
Say what the result is: a Tier 2 own candidate, not an observation of a flood, not validated, verify before action.

what_a_change_notice_must_say: that FloodGuard changed the data, and each step above with the values of that file
the credit line: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2024
the two acquisition times, so that a reader sees the second scene is of 16 September 2024, 06:16 in Thailand, after the flood peak
the label of the result (Tier 2 own candidate; verify before action)
change_notice.basis: The provider's notice, as the repository records it, asks for the credit line for adapted data. The itemised change notice is FloodGuard's own rule for every derived layer, modelled on the product 4009 record. It is a caution, not a term of the notice and not legal advice.

use_in_this_track: keep the two original archives outside Git and read them there
calibrate, geocode and resample both scenes, compare the two dates and classify the change (plan tasks A2 and A4)
load the resulting radar candidates as Tier 2 flood inputs of case O1 (floodguard.flood_inputs.load_o1, plan task E1), with the credit line and a change notice in every layer
compute tables for the eight Mae Sai tambons and statistics for whole areas from them, each with the credit line
rank the change in backscatter against other layers in the diagnosis of plan task A1, which reads the stored sigma0 rasters of the same two scenes

would_allow_once_confirmed_and_registere.uses: The five uses listed under use_in_this_track, and nothing else.
would_allow_once_confirmed_and_registere.rights_level_basis: floodguard.rights gives the level local to every confirmed record that is not the product 4009 record: such a record 'states no publication scope', so the input is read and processed outside Git and nothing derived from it is written into public web files. A request for a public write through the registry would still be refused.
would_allow_once_confirmed_and_registere.what_changes_for_case_O1: floodguard.flood_inputs.load_o1 would accept a radar candidate whose receipt names this record, instead of refusing every candidate. Open point E1-OP2 would close for the two scenes.
would_allow_once_confirmed_and_registere.what_does_not_change: Case O1 still cannot be scored that day. The radar candidates have not been delivered to plan task E1 in the form its loader reads, the geocoding of record is open (A4-OP1), the planning-assessment builder does not read a radar candidate yet, and the candidate table records the Tier 2 skill bar as not met at Mae Sai, so every O1 row would be low confidence and class E under class rule v1.

publication_scope.what_the_recorded_terms_would_support: The repository records that the notice permits distribution and communication to the public of adapted data with the credit line. The owners check that against the provider's page before they rely on it.

options.text: Confirm the record for the uses above at the local level only. Nothing changes in the code beyond adding the record to the registry. Layers and per-tambon tables made from the scenes stay outside public web files.

Confirm the record and also name a publication scope: layers, tables and figures made from the two scenes may be published with the credit line and a change notice, each labelled as a Tier 2 own candidate. This needs a new version of this record that states the scope, and a reviewed change to floodguard.rights so that the registry reads the scope from it. Until that change is merged, the level stays local.

publication_scope.pitch_level: Not offered: no rights record of the repository says what a pitch-level use is, and the registry never assigns that level.
publication_scope.note: Neither option is chosen here. A recommendation is not a decision.

would_not_allow: any use before both owners confirm the record and it is added to floodguard.rights.REGISTERED_RECORDS
a write under apps/web/public/ of anything made from the two scenes (the level is local under today's code)

any other Sentinel-1 scene or copy: the passes of 6 and 18 September 2024, the copies of the 6 and 15 September passes that the replay reads, and any new download (protocol v1b lists the 18 September pass as download DL-4, which is not approved)
the Sentinel-1 images the Mae Sai replay shows: they are published under the replay's own source list, and this record changes nothing about them
the training data of the A6-prime classifier (the GEOID-Flood sample): the second half of open point E1-OP2 asks whether it needs a record of its own, and this record does not answer that
any third-party flood map or reference product, whatever satellite it was made from
use as machine-learning labels, as a qualified reference, or as a check of how correct another layer is
any statement that a radar candidate is an observation of a flood or a basis for an operational decision; a candidate is not an official warning

for_the_owners: The committed acquisition manifest marks both archives processing_allowed False, because the status of a reference mask was unresolved in July. Decision R14 says that this note gates the finals baseline only, not rights, and allows the replay to read the 3 September archive. R14 does not name plan tasks A2 and A4 or the 15 September archive. Please say whether the same reading holds for them (open point A4-OP5). If it does not, this record should not be confirmed as drafted.
Please open the provider's page named under licence and check the five points listed there. Correct the record and the notice where the page says something else.
Please choose option A or B under publication_scope. Option B needs more work before it has any effect.
Please read the limits. Then follow owner_confirmation.how_to_confirm, or say what should change.
limitations: This is a draft by an AI coding agent. No owner has read it, and no provider page was opened when it was written.
The record covers two archives, identified by name, size and SHA-256. A file with another SHA-256 is not covered.
The repository does not record the download of the two archives: the committed manifest marks download_attempted False for both and names nobody who downloaded them.
The legal notice gives no warranty of fitness. A radar candidate is a Tier 2 own candidate: it is not an observation of a flood and it is not validated. Nothing was checked against a reference.
The second scene was taken on 16 September 2024 at 06:16 in Thailand, several days after the flood peak. A candidate made from the pair is residual water at that pass at most.

The layers of the run of record are displaced by about 680 m and its two dates are offset from each other by about 9 m (outputs/planning_v1/README.md, open point A4-OP1). A rights record changes nothing about that.

The radar tables and the diagnosis figures made from the two scenes were committed on 4 October 2026 with the credit line, before this draft existed. This record does not say whether that was within the rules; the owners do.
The Thai half of the notice file was written by the AI coding agent and was not reviewed by a native speaker (decision R18; roadmap item H12 is unsigned).
This record is not legal advice.
assumptions: The two archives on disk are the products the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem distributes under the catalogue product ids above. Their SHA-256 and size are the ones the committed acquisition manifest and both radar receipts record.
The legal notice at the address above is the notice that governs the two products, as docs/reference_mask_licensing_log.md records it.
The terms have not changed since 20 July 2026 in a way that matters for the uses listed. The owners check this.
A radar candidate made from the two scenes is adapted data, so it carries the credit line for modified data.
confidence_reason: The two archives are identified by name, size and SHA-256 in a committed receipt and in the committed acquisition manifest, and the repository records a check of the provider's pages on 20 July 2026. No provider page was opened for this draft, the form of the credit line is to be checked, and no owner has read the record.

decision_refs.summary: The replay may read the 3 September 2024 Sentinel-1 archive; the July acquisition note 'processing_allowed False / do not run baseline yet' gates the finals baseline only, not rights. R14 does not name plan tasks A2 and A4 or the 15 September archive.
The radar answers of 3 October 2026. They concern the benchmark and the skill bar, not rights.
The supervised radar classifier is deferred until Mae Sai is complete, so its training data is not part of this record.
Extra Sentinel-1 dates need an existing Earth Engine account or one download that the owner approves first. No extra date is part of this record.

signed_decision_note: No row of the decision log records a decision on the rights of Sentinel-1 data. When the owners confirm this record, a new row is added after R18 and named here, with the date, both names and how the confirmation was given.

owner_confirmation.note: Nobody has confirmed this record. It was drafted on 5 October 2026 and has not been shown to either owner.
owner_confirmation.how_to_confirm: Both owners read this file and the notice file, check the provider's pages named under licence, answer the first question under for_the_owners and choose option A or B under publication_scope. Then, in one change: set owner_confirmation.status to confirmed, list both names in confirmed_by, set confirmed_on (YYYY-MM-DD), set record_status to confirmed and record_status_text to match, set signed_by_human and human_rights_clearance to true, fill signed_decision with the new decision-log row, replace the draft status lines of the notice file, and add the row to the decision log. A separate, reviewed change then adds the record to floodguard.rights.REGISTERED_RECORDS as a record of copernicus_sentinel1 and updates the tests that say no such record exists. Until both changes are merged, the code refuses every radar candidate of case O1.

registration.note: The record is not in floodguard.rights.REGISTERED_RECORDS and no code reads this file. tests/test_owner_unblocker_records.py fails if the record is registered, or says it is confirmed, while its confirmation is pending.
